b2-08-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Even If It Rains
b2-08-01.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos says it may rain on Saturday in Budapest. You will go out anyway.
b2-08-01.prompt: Tell Carlos you will go out even if it rains.
cues: Say that you will go out
Say that you will go even if it rains
b2-08-01.target: Aunque llueva el sábado, voy a salir.
b2-08-01.english: Even if it rains on Saturday, I'm going to go out.
b2-08-01.canDo: I can use aunque with the indicative for a fact and with the subjunctive for a possibility or a point I grant.

b2-08-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Granting a Point
b2-08-02.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks what you think of a proposal at your office. It is expensive, but it has advantages.
b2-08-02.prompt: Tell Meg what you think of the proposal, in a formal way.
cues: Grant that the proposal is expensive
b2-08-02.target: Si bien la propuesta es cara, tiene muchas ventajas.
b2-08-02.english: Although the proposal is expensive, it has many advantages.
b2-08-02.canDo: I can grant a true point formally with si bien and the indicative.

b2-08-03.title: Communicative Challenge: No Matter How Much
b2-08-03.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos keeps asking you to change your mind about something. You will not change it.
b2-08-03.prompt: Tell Carlos that his insisting will not change your mind.
cues: Say that he can insist as much as he wants
Say that you will not change your mind
b2-08-03.target: Por más que insistas, no voy a cambiar de idea.
b2-08-03.english: However much you insist, I'm not going to change my mind.
b2-08-03.canDo: I can say that no amount of effort changes the result, using por más que and por mucho que with the subjunctive.

b2-08-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Even When It Is Difficult
b2-08-04.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks if you will tell your colleagues the truth about a problem. It will be difficult, but you will do it.
b2-08-04.prompt: Tell Meg that you will tell the truth, even if it is difficult.
cues: Say that you are going to tell the truth
Say that you will do it even if it is difficult
b2-08-04.target: Aun cuando sea difícil, vamos a decir la verdad.
b2-08-04.english: Even if it is difficult, we are going to tell the truth.
b2-08-04.canDo: I can use aun cuando with the subjunctive for a possibility and with the indicative for a fact.

b2-08-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Whatever Happens
b2-08-05.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos is worried about a project at his office. You promise to support him.
b2-08-05.prompt: Tell Carlos that you will support him whatever happens.
cues: Say that you will support him
Say that it does not matter what happens
b2-08-05.target: Pase lo que pase, te voy a apoyar.
b2-08-05.english: Whatever happens, I'm going to support you.
b2-08-05.canDo: I can say that nothing changes my decision with formulas such as pase lo que pase and diga lo que diga.

b2-08-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Keeping Your Position
b2-08-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks if you will finish the report today. You have a lot of work, but you will finish it.
b2-08-consolidation.prompt: Tell Meg that you will finish the report today in spite of the work.
cues: Say that you have a lot of work
Say that you will finish the report today anyway
b2-08-consolidation.target: Aunque tengo mucho trabajo, voy a terminar el informe hoy.
b2-08-consolidation.english: Although I have a lot of work, I'm going to finish the report today.
b2-08-consolidation.canDo: I can concede a point and keep my position with aunque, si bien, por más que and aun cuando.
